# TokenCalculator.dev

TokenCalculator.dev is a free, privacy-first, browser-based LLM token calculator covering OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot Kimi, xAI Grok, Z.ai GLM, and Meta. Unlike text-only token counters, it accepts pasted prompts together with readable documents, source/data files, and supported images, then reports provider token counts, context-window fit, and API cost estimates. Zero prompt text, document contents, or uploaded images are sent to a calculation server.

## Accuracy

OpenAI text is tokenized exactly, in the browser, with the model's own BPE encoding. Every other provider family uses a deterministic UTF-8 byte-length projection and is labelled "estimated" rather than "exact". Image tokens use each provider's published tile or patch formula, and report as unsupported when a provider does not publish one. Rates are regenerated from a public model catalogue and carry the date they were verified.

## Developer API and local SDK

**Base URL: `https://tokencalculator.dev/api/v1` - no API key, no registration, no signup.**

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute, per IP, per route. A 429 response carries `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-*` headers. CORS is open (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`), so browser-based agents can call it directly.

Endpoints:

- `GET /api/v1/models` - every supported model id with context window and verified per-million-token rates. Cacheable, returns an `ETag`.
- `GET /api/v1/health` - liveness check.
- `POST /api/v1/count` - measure one request.
- `POST /api/v1/batch` - measure up to 25 requests in one call.
- `POST /api/v1/compare` - run one input across up to 10 models.

Copy-paste example:

```bash
curl -X POST https://tokencalculator.dev/api/v1/count \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6-terra","input":{"text":"Hello world"},"output_tokens":100}'
```

Common vendor names such as `gpt-4o`, `claude-3-5-sonnet`, `gemini-1.5-pro` and `deepseek-chat` are resolved to the nearest supported model, so a first guess at a model id usually works. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents; branch on the `type` URI, which is distinct per error class.

- [Free developer API and playground](https://tokencalculator.dev/developers/api/)
- [Developer API reference](https://tokencalculator.dev/docs/api/)
- [OpenAPI 3.1 contract](https://tokencalculator.dev/openapi.json)
- [Local npm core package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jay0073/tokencalculator-core)

The public HTTP API measures text, chat messages, already-extracted file or source-code contents, and image geometry across supported models. It can return token usage, per-part breakdowns, cost, context-window utilization, calculation methods, verified pricing, batch results, and multi-model comparisons. HTTP payloads necessarily reach the TokenCalculator.dev edge Worker; use the browser calculator or `@jay0073/tokencalculator-core` for privacy-first local processing of confidential prompts, documents, and code.

OpenAI raw text uses exact local BPE tokenization. Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek use TokenCalculator.dev's deterministic Provider-Calibrated UTF-8 Token Projection: UTF-8 byte length normalized by a provider-family bytes-per-token coefficient. Supported image counts use provider-published patch, tile, detail, and cap formulas. Provider API usage remains authoritative.

## Documents and images

- Text documents: TXT, Markdown, CSV, JSON, common source-code formats, HTML, XML, YAML, TOML, SQL, and shell scripts.
- Rich documents: readable PDF and DOCX text is extracted locally. Scanned PDFs require OCR and are not supported.
- Images: PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF dimensions are read locally. OpenAI, Claude, and Gemini visual tokens use documented provider formulas; unsupported models are reported as unavailable.
- Combined workloads: pasted text, extracted file text, and supported image tokens are added into the same model result and cost projection.
- File limit: 12 MB per file.
- Privacy: processing is browser-only. No prompt, file contents, or image pixels are sent to TokenCalculator.dev for calculation.
- Enterprise use: confidential system prompts, internal documents, proprietary source code, logs, and datasets can be preflighted without uploading their contents to a separate token-counting service.
- Network boundary: public pricing metadata and privacy-disclosed analytics may be requested, but neither receives submitted content, derived token counts, or cost results.

## Tokenization methods

| Provider | Browser method | Accuracy label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `o200k_base` BPE via js-tiktoken | Exact for raw text under that encoding |
| Anthropic Claude | Provider-Calibrated UTF-8 Token Projection | Deterministic provider-family projection |
| Google Gemini | Provider-Calibrated UTF-8 Token Projection | Deterministic projection; Gemini `countTokens` is authoritative |
| DeepSeek | Provider-Calibrated UTF-8 Token Projection | Deterministic provider-family projection |

The site does not claim access to proprietary Claude, Gemini, or DeepSeek production tokenizers. API wrappers, tools, system instructions, reasoning tokens, and provider-side processing can change billed usage.
